title: TOS eval case
_comment: ONE schema, because there were six. 75 cases were authored across 18 skills in FOUR mutually incompatible dialects (prompt/assertions · command/assert · input/assert · intent/expect); the 43 atom stubs prescribed a FIFTH shape ({id, input, expected_output_shape, must_contain, must_not_contain}) that zero cases use; and tools/skill-template/evals/evals.json is a SIXTH (trigger_evals, with `evals: []` and no example). Four dialects cannot share a runner, which is a large part of why no eval had ever been executed. `kind` is the discriminator: `command` and `call` are deterministic and RUN in CI via tools/run_evals.py; `prompt` is model-facing and is NEVER executed there — its evidence is recorded under benchmarks/. Anything that claims to be executable must actually be executable, or it is honestly labelled `prompt`.

kind.description: command = run an allow-listed argv and assert on its output · call = import an in-repo callable and assert on its return · prompt = model-facing, recorded not executed

command.description: kind=command. argv0 must be an allow-listed interpreter. An unfilled <placeholder> makes the case SKIP with a reason, never pass.

call.description: kind=call. `module.path:function`, resolved with shared/ and tools/ on sys.path.

input.description: kind=call. Passed to the callable; use `kwargs: true` to splat a dict.

assert.description: kind=command|call. Plain keys and dotted paths (`required_cadence.authority`) read the parsed output. Reserved meta-keys: `has` (list of keys that must be present), `each.<listkey>` (every item of that list carries these keys), `stdout_contains` (substrings of raw stdout — the only honest form for a tool that emits prose), `exit_code`. A string value beginning >=, <=, >, < or != is a comparison; a list compares order-insensitively; a bool is compared by identity, so 1 does NOT satisfy true.

assertions.description: kind=prompt. Prose, judged by a human or a blind judge — never machine-checked. Saying so is the point.

evidence.description: kind=prompt. Repo-relative path to a recorded run under benchmarks/results/. Absent = unrun, which is a visible gap, not a pass.

trigger_evals.description: Routing tests: does THIS skill activate on prompts it should own, and stay quiet on prompts it should not? Behaviour cases test the skill AFTER invocation; these test the description's triggering. The template has mandated >=10 positive / >=5 negative 'before shipping' since it was written, and 61 of 62 skills shipped without any.

graded_by.description: `router` = shared/routing/router.py, deterministic and offline, so atom trigger evals need no model. `model` = requires a recorded run.

instead.description: negatives only: the skill that SHOULD own this, or 'out of ecosystem'.
